title: Gamma runway + hire slab sensitivity journal
body:
Purpose:
Quick working workbook to capture an operations-friendly headcount phasing + pricing sensitivity sweep tied to SKU/job slabs. This is intentionally lightweight — combine with the main budget model after we pick a preferred scenario.

Context / why this is different:
- We need a fast way to map a small incremental price change to hiring cadence (sprint-level) and runway impact, but bucketed by SKU (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and by region.
- The deliverable is a lab notebook: scenario notes, assumptions, a compact month-by-month lo-fi table, and immediate flags for product/GTM.

Key assumptions (work-in-progress):
1) Baseline revenue / token mix (global blended): 60% hosted, 25% dedicated, 15% private.
2) Average tokens per billable request = 780 tokens.
3) Unit gross margin assumptions by SKU (pre-hc): hosted 55%, dedicated 48%, private 60%.
4) Current blended price (per 1k tokens equivalent): $0.80.
5) Hiring ramp targets measured in FTE-equivalents; one infra/ops FTE supports ~150k M tokens/month throughput (sustained) at current batching/utilization.
6) GPU-cost tailwinds / quantization: expected 6% op-cost reduction if quantization adoption hits 40% of hosted volume.
7) FX/regional premium: APAC priced at +8% list in our model, EMEA neutral.

Scenarios (three sketches):
- Scenario A (Baseline / committed): keep list price, hire as-plan: +9 FTE over next 6 months (3 infra, 2 SRE, 2 eng-server, 2 sales-ops).
- Scenario B (Conservative): price +5% across hosted SKUs, delay hire +3 months -> net runway extension but may suppress demand 3–6% (elasticity).
- Scenario C (Aggressive growth push): price -7% to capture volume, frontload hiring +6 FTE this quarter to avoid throttles; risk: margin compression and higher GPU spot exposure.

Sensitivity parameters to sweep (these are the knobs):
- price_delta_pct = [-10, -7, -5, 0, +5, +10]
- demand_elasticity = [-1.1, -0.6, -0.25] (i.e., percent volume change per percent price change; negative means demand increases when price falls)
- quantization_adoption = [10, 40, 70] % (affects op-costs)
- hire_delay_months = [0, 3, 6]

Mini-run (example calculation):
Inputs (example): baseline monthly billings = $8.4M; blended price per 1M tokens = $800; monthly token consumption = 10.5B tokens.
If price_delta = +5% -> immediate revenue uplift +5% (assume short-run demand hit 0% elastic for hosted -> conservative).
Net effect: revenue -> $8.82M. But margin: op-costs unchanged so gross margin expands slightly. Hiring: we delay hiring 3 months; payroll savings this quarter ~ $135k (9 FTE avg fully loaded $45k/month each across hires? adjust).

Table (lo-fi text) — month columns (M0..M5) (values are illustrative):
Month | Headcount net change | Monthly payroll delta | Expected tokens (B) | Revenue ($M) | Runway days delta
M0 | +2 | +90k | 10.5 | 8.4 | 0
M1 | +3 | +135k | 11.1 | 8.8 | -2
M2 | +1 | +45k | 11.7 | 9.2 | -4
M3 | 0 (delay pickup) | 0 | 11.2 | 9.0 | +6
M4 | +2 (catchup) | +90k | 11.9 | 9.6 | -3
M5 | 0 | 0 | 12.0 | 9.7 | -1

Notes on the table: runway days delta is against our baseline runway (90 days). Small hires frontloading reduces runway; delaying adds runway.

Headcount phasing by role (preferred baseline):
- Infra: +3 (M0..M2) — staggered hiring to keep ramp overhead lower.
- SRE: +2 (M1..M3).
- Serving-engineering: +2 (M0..M1) urgent to unlock throughput gains.
- Sales-ops / Solutions: +2 (M2..M3) tie to dedicated deals.

Pricing sensitivity quick-calcs (per 1% price change):
- If elasticity = -0.6 and price change = -7% then volume change = +4.2% -> revenue change = (-7% + 4.2%) = -2.8% net (i.e., revenue down).
- If quantization adoption lifts from 10% to 40% in 3 months, operations cost drop = 6% of op-cost slice => margin uplift ~ 1.8 percentage points (rough estimate).

Risks and open questions (action items):
- Q1: evidence for short-run elasticity by SKU/segment. Ask growth/data to compute elasticities by cohort (hosted vs dedicated). (JIRA: JIRA-FIN-987)
- Q2: clarity on FTE fully-loaded assumptions (benchmarks vary). Current model uses $180k/year fully-loaded for infra; confirm with People Ops.
- Q3: customer churn sensitivity if we increase hosted list price +10% (worst-case). Need to run a cohort lift analysis.
- Q4: quantify backlog risk if hiring frontloads too fast and we cannot deploy new capacity due to infra debt. Coordinate with Eng-Release.

Immediate recommendations for finance + product (short actionable list):
- Run a 6x6 grid in the main budget workbook: price_delta x hire_delay. Output metrics: delta runway days, delta gross margin, delta net cash burn.
- Prioritize getting a hosted-SKU short-run elasticity estimate from growth (target: within 7 days).
- Prepare a soft-commit hiring window: tie hires to metric triggers (e.g., sustained 5% QoQ token growth for 2 weeks) so we can decouple price experiments from hires.

Scratch calculations (put these into the model later):
- FTE monthly fully-loaded = $15,000 (baseline) -> annual $180k.
- GPU opex per 1B tokens = $12k (baseline) -> if quantization adoption hits 40% reduce to $11.3k per 1B tokens (6% saving on the GPU slice).
- Break-even price delta to sustain one additional infra FTE: additional infra FTE cost per month = $15k -> needed incremental monthly revenue at 55% margin = 15k / 0.55 = ~$27.3k -> in 1M-token-price units (baseline $800 per 1M) that's 34.1k tokens ~ 0.0341M tokens. So tiny relative to platform volumes but flagged because hiring introduces headcount step costs and lead time.

Paper trail / where to land final outputs:
- Push the scenario outputs into: CONFLUENCE-4532 (token-econ playbook) + the main budget workbook (link will be created).
- Create a short slide (1–2 slides) for the ELT finance review summarizing: preferred scenario, runway impact, and gating triggers.

Todo checklist (short):
- [ ] Growth: elasticity by SKU (hosted/dedicated/private) — due 2026-05-27
- [ ] People Ops: confirm fully-loaded FTE range per role — due 2026-05-24
- [ ] Eng: feasibility note on front-loading infra hires (deploy cadence risks) — due 2026-05-26
- [ ] Finance: run the 6x6 grid and add outputs to the workbook — due 2026-05-28

Quick log of iteration changes:
- 2026-03-02: initial sketch and assumptions (created)
- 2026-04-15: added quantization savings assumption after infra review
- 2026-05-20: baseline numbers adjusted to reflect updated bookings cadence

Owner/next steps: Elena Kim (finance) — maintain this as the working journal for headcount-price sensitivity experiments until we converge on a single scenario to fold into FY planning.

Freeform notes (notes-to-self):
- Keep the hire triggers conservative. We can always opportunistically hire contractors but making permanent FTE decisions should map to >2 independent signals (token growth + committed pipeline + margin buffer).
- Consider a small pilot price-band experiment (A/B test across 3% price delta) and measure short-run elasticities before a full roll.

End of journal entry.
